name: Guillotine Choke from Hindulotine
summary: The Guillotine Choke encloses the neck from the front with a choking arm and supporting hand, using head control and body position to remove space before pressure is applied.
description: Guillotine Choke from Hindulotine changes the neck enclosure. Clear the raised leg and establish the standard choking arm and supporting hand separately.
overview:
The attacker is in front of a lowered head, with the choking arm around the neck and a stable standing or guard connection. Hindu Control includes a raised leg in the enclosure. An ordinary guillotine requires deliberate re-gripping and leg clearance; a shared word in the names does not make the grips interchangeable.

Establish a chin-strap or equivalent front head control without twisting the jaw. Bring the forearm into the neck space while keeping the head aligned. Secure the selected grip without pulling the head backward. Use a stable base or guard connection so the opponent cannot freely circle around the choke.

Use slow enclosure practice and avoid cervical extension or twisting. Open the hands and remove the neck restraint immediately on any tap.

Instructional sources: [Rob Biernacki and Stephan Kesting — guillotine control](https://www.grapplearts.com/guillotine-choke/); [Ben Eddy — Hindu Control to Hindulotine](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Y5ZQNgG2hNc).

attacker.overview:
The attacker is in front of a lowered head, with the choking arm around the neck and a stable standing or guard connection. Hindu Control includes a raised leg in the enclosure. Establish a chin-strap or equivalent front head control without twisting the jaw. Bring the forearm into the neck space while keeping the head aligned. Secure the selected grip without pulling the head backward.

Use a stable base or guard connection so the opponent cannot freely circle around the choke. Use the torso and elbows to remove slack; reset if the pressure becomes a neck crank. Open both hands and remove body pressure immediately on a tap.

Use slow enclosure practice and avoid cervical extension or twisting. Open the hands and remove the neck restraint immediately on any tap.

If the opponent clears your legs to the weak side, stop trying to finish the guillotine. Turn onto your side before a crossface and shoulder pressure pin the upper body; check the near knee or hip with the free hand as hip movement makes room to return your bottom knee inside. Keep the remaining neck connection unloaded while recovering that guard space.

flashcards.question: Guillotine practice: after the choke is lost to a weak-side pass, which barrier helps recover guard?
flashcards.answer: An inside bottom knee behind a shoulder frame. Once the choke has opened, the reviewed weak-side recovery uses a side angle, protection from the crossface and recovery of the bottom knee. It is a guard-recovery phase, not a renewed squeeze from the lost grip.
flashcards.answer_line: Inside knee behind a shoulder frame

plausible: Both hands chase head, knees outside
Neck crank after they clear the legs
trap: Flat torso, elbow away from knee
